markdown_content: ## Modular Library Update Overview This section explains the recent update to Clo’s modular library system, focusing on the consolidation into a single modular library. It covers how the update affects old modular blocks, file compatibility, and key user settings to manage modular assets efficiently. --- ## Consolidation of Modular Libraries into One Clo has optimized its modular system by merging all modular libraries into a single, unified modular library. This change eliminates confusion about which library a block belongs to, simplifying access. Users can now access modular blocks for categories such as kids, men, and women all within one library. Additionally, users can create and add their own modular blocks easily. Key points: - Only one modular library is used now. - Modular blocks are organized by category within this single library. - Existing tutorials on modular provide comprehensive guidance on usage. --- ## Handling Legacy Modular Files When importing files created with older versions of Clo’s modular libraries, a pop-up notification informs users that the file originates from an older modular library. Despite this, Clo will load the modular file automatically and maintain its modular properties. Important details: - The old modular blocks will load correctly but will not automatically be placed in the new modular library. - Users must manually assign the imported modular blocks to appropriate categories within the new library. - This manual organization prevents misplacement of modular blocks (e.g., pants accidentally saved in shirts). --- ## Setting Default Modular Library Save Location Users can specify a default folder location for saving modular blocks, improving file organization and workflow efficiency. This setting is accessible via: **User Settings > Other > Modular Library** Features: - Set a default directory for modular files (e.g., a “testing modular” folder on the desktop). - Useful for individuals and large teams needing centralized storage. - New modular blocks will default to this folder unless manually changed. --- ## Saving and Categorizing Modular Blocks When saving a modular block, users select the category (e.g., men’s, women’s, kids) in which to save the file. The save dialog will default to the previously set folder location. Steps: 1. Choose **File > Save As**. 2. Select or create a category folder (e.g., men’s, women’s, kids, or custom). 3. Assign the modular block to a category folder within the default directory. 4. Confirm save location. This process ensures modular blocks are stored logically and retrievably. --- ## Creating and Adding Modular Block Components Users can add various modular components to a block, such as: - Front Body - Back Body - Sleeves - Collar - Cuffs Procedure: - Select each component and add it to the modular block. - Optionally, add images or custom elements to each component. - After assembling components, validate taglines and metadata. - Save the modular block to the designated category folder. This modular component system enables flexible garment design and detailed customization. --- ## Accessing Saved Modular Blocks Once saved, modular blocks are accessible both within Clo’s modular library interface and via the file system in the designated folder. Example: - Browse to the default folder on the desktop (e.g., “Testing Modular > Practice > Button Down Shirts”). - All modular blocks saved in this folder structure are available immediately for use. This dual access supports seamless design iteration and file management. --- ## Summary of Workflow for Using Modular Library Update 1. Import old modular files—Clo will notify and load them but requires manual categorization. 2. Set a default save location in User Settings to centralize modular files. 3. When saving modular blocks, assign them to appropriate categories within the default folder. 4. Add modular components as needed and verify metadata before saving. 5. Access saved modular blocks through Clo or directly in the file system. This workflow enhances modular file management and improves clarity in modular garment design. --- ## Important Notes and Caveats - Old modular files do not automatically migrate into the new single modular library structure; manual categorization is necessary to maintain order. - Setting a default save folder is highly recommended to avoid scattered files. - Modular components must be explicitly added and validated before saving for proper functionality. - The modular library update supports existing modular files but requires some user action to integrate older content fully. --- This document serves as a detailed guide to understanding and leveraging the new modular library update in Clo, ensuring users can efficiently manage modular garment components and files.
